This vignette contains a reproducible example of knittogether. The code can be copied into a .R, .rmd, or .qmd file should you wish to run it locally.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Vignette reproducibility

To make this vignette fully reproducible the following files are created through code, though typically would be made manually with other software:

-   **word.docx**: A Word document containing all the basic features knittogether supports (e.g. an image, table, and citations) and some placeholders. This is created by via a Quarto document.

-   **child.qmd**: A Quarto file that contains some of the code to replace one of the placeholders with.

-   **bibliography.bib**: A file containing the reference details of the citation.

These are stored in a temporary directory and this is reflected in the file paths being wrapped in `file.path(temp_dir, file).` This is not needed for normal usage.

The code to create the files is below and includes an option for docx and pptx. Note for pptx pandoc 3.8.3 or higher is required.

```{r setup}
#| code-fold: true
library(pandoc)
library(withr)
# Use a temporary working directory for this vignette
temp_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "knittogether_vignette_workflow")
dir.create(temp_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# This function allows for easy recreation of a starting state to use knittogether from
create_base_files <- function(output = "docx", child_qmd = TRUE, image = TRUE, bib = TRUE, render) {
  
  if(child_qmd) {
  child_qmd <- paste(
    "## Content from a child qmd",
    "",
    "```{r}",
    "plot(1, 1)",
    "```",
    "",
    "The addition of 1 and 1 is `r 1+1`.",
    "",
    sep = "\n")

  writeLines(child_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "child_example.qmd"))
  }

  if(image) {
  png(file.path(temp_dir, "image.png"), width = 600, height = 400)
  x <- 1:10
  plot(x, x^2, type = "b", col = "blue", pch = 19,
       main = "Example Image Created in R", xlab = "X values", ylab = "Y values (squared)")
  dev.off()
  }
  
  if(bib) {
  bib <- ("@book{roseRosesStrategyPreventive2008,
          title = {Rose's {{Strategy}} of {{Preventive Medicine}}},
          author = {Rose, Geoffrey},
          year = 2008,
          month = jan,
          publisher = {OUP Oxford},
          abstract = {},
          isbn = {978-0-19-101559-5}
          }"
          )
    
    writeLines(bib, file.path(temp_dir, "example.bib"))
  }
  
  if(output == "docx") {
  example_qmd <- r"(
---
title: "Example Word Document"
subtitle: "This document is used as a knittogether example"
format: docx
---

# Introduction

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.[@roseRosesStrategyPreventive2008]

![Fig 1. A plot](image.png){fig-alt="A image"}

## More info

  -   Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.
  -   Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
  -   Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

# Main content

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit. placeholder_content_total.

  1.  Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
      1.  In id cursus mi pretium tellus duis convallis.
  2.  Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

| Col1 | Col2 | Col3 |
|------|------|------|
| A    | 1    | 4    |
| B    | 2    | 5    |
| C    | 3    | 6    |

: Table 1. This is a table

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

placeholder_content_childqmd

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

placeholder_content_1x1plot

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

The number of rows in the data set is placeholder_content_mtcarsrows.
)"
  
  writeLines(example_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"))
  
  if(render) {
    pandoc::pandoc_run(c(file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"), "-f", 
                         "markdown", "-o", file.path(temp_dir, "example.docx")))
    }
  } else if(output == "pptx") {
    example_qmd <- r"(
---
title: "Example PowerPoint Presentation"
subtitle: "This presentation is used as a knittogether example"
format: pptx
---

# Introduction
  
## Background

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.

# Main Content

## Dinner

  -   Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.
  -   Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
  -   Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit. placeholder_content_total.

  1.  Quisque faucibus ex sapien vitae pellentesque sem placerat.
      1.  In id cursus mi pretium tellus duis convallis.
  2.  Tempus leo eu aenean sed diam urna tempor.

## A plot

placeholder_content_1x1plot

)"
  
  writeLines(example_qmd, file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"))
    
    if(render) {
      pandoc::pandoc_run(c(file.path(temp_dir, "example.qmd"), "-f", 
                           "markdown", "-o", file.path(temp_dir, "example.pptx")))
      }
  }
}

create_base_files(output = "docx")
```
:::

### Convert

Here the input file (in this case a .docx) will be converted into a markdown file. The image found in the docx is also produced into a folder called `media/`.

```{r convert}
knittogether::convert(input_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.docx"),
                      markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"), 
                      media_base_dir = file.path(temp_dir, "workflow"),
                      pandoc_version = "default", )
```

In this case the contents of the Word document are relatively simple. If for instance the document contained a table with very long text or line breaks then other `pandoc_args` may need to be passed such as a command to use GitHub Flavored Markdown (`-t gfm`). If required the `pandoc::pandoc_run()` function can be used to fully specify the conversion options. Note that these can have knock on effects that mean the markdown requires further cleaning to be processed correctly.

### Clean

If required cleaning can be performed. In this case

-   `heading_offset` is used to demote headers down a level because level 1 headings in Word are converted to level 1 headings in HTML, which are typically reserved for page titles.

-   `clean_citations` is used to remove the excess `/` when importing citations.

```{r clean}
knittogether::clean(markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"),
                    heading_offset = T,
                    clean_citations = T)
```

If working with a file generated through knittogether, options such as `clear_draft` and `clear_placeholder_styling` may be useful. Further detail about these options is available in the `clean()` documentation.

### Replace

The bulk of `knittogether`'s activity is in the `replace()` function. This handles switching the placeholders with the relevant code-generated content.

First, the code-based content must be created. This content can either be a scalar (a single named value such as `value = 42`) or non-scalar (a list as created by `define_content()`). This content is brought together into a single list with `placeholder_map()`. For example:

```{r content}
# Example with a child quarto document
child <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "A plot in a child qmd",
  placeholder_id = "childqmd",
  output_mode = "chunk",
  content = "{{< include child_example.qmd >}}",
  content_type = "plot",
  chunk_options = list(engine = "r", as_child = TRUE, 
                       child_dir = "children", echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7))

# Example with a function
plot <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "A plot",
  placeholder_id = "1x1plot",
  output_mode = "chunk", 
  content = { plot(1, 1) },
  content_type = "plot",
  chunk_options  = list(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 7))

# Example of inline content
inline <- knittogether::define_content(
  description = "Number of rows in mtcars",
  placeholder_id = "mtcarsrows",
  output_mode = "inline",
  content = { nrow(mtcars) },
  content_type = "text")

map <- knittogether::placeholder_map(
  specs = list(child, plot, inline),
  scalars = list(total = 42)
)
```

Scalars are quick to define but have limited scope as they must be inline text and lack the validation checks that non-scalar content has like descriptions.

When using child documents, be conscious of relative paths. To avoid errors, keep the parent qmd, input file (docx or pptx), processed markdown output, and a folder of child qmds in the same directory. Care also needs to be taken to ensure the variables required to evaluate code are available in the context in which it is evaluated (i.e., child qmds need access to variables called within them). If data is needed across multiple child qmds, consider using `{{< include data_processing.qmd >}}` in multiple child qmds.

The contents and map are passed to the `replace()` function which handles matching the content to the placeholders. Options such as `draft_mode` and `marker_mode` can be supplied which allow bookending this inserted content with markers to allow easy replacement when it is read back in (for instance "The inline value is --DRAFT_CONTENT-- placeholder_total 42 --END_DRAFT_CONTENT--").

```{r replace}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false

knittogether::replace(
  markdown_file = file.path(temp_dir, "example.md"),
  placeholder_prefix = "placeholder_content",
  validation_path = file.path(temp_dir, "validation"),
  code_content = map,
  draft_mode = F,
  marker_mode = "off"
)
```

The markdown document now includes the code-based content specified.

````{=html}
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

{{\< include children/child_childqmd.qmd >}}

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

```{r 1x1plot, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=7}
{
    plot(1, 1)
}
```

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipiscing elit.

The number of rows in the data set is `r { nrow(mtcars) }`.
````

### Output

Finally, the markdown can be included in a qmd file (for example through `{{< include workflow/example.qmd >}}`) which can be rendered in the relevant format, now including the code-based content.

If output to Word or PowerPoint, the resulting file can be altered and read back into using `knittogether` again if required to add new or update existing code-based content (provided `draft_mode` has been used).

For long content rendered to website or book format, it may be preferable to split the content across multiple pages. Ordinarily, this would require separate files to be created, each with relevant content so they appear on the [sidebar](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-navigation.html#side-navigation). The [quarto-external](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-external) extension provides a method of extracting only a section of an input file. For instance, an almost empty qmd could be created for each page with `{{< external <file>#<section> >}}` added to include a specific section from the single markdown file generated through knittogether. If preferred, content can be manually copied or a script set up to split the markdown.

### Validate

Additionally `replace()` creates outputs that can be used to check the right code has been applied to the right placeholder and highlight any changes in the code. A csv log is created and, optionally, this can also be placed into a html file containing a `reactable` table allowing easier navigation of the information in the csv.

It can be beneficial to add more, smaller placeholders so that descriptions of content can be more specific and validation more precise.

### Next steps

You can `split()` a single extracted `.md` / `.qmd` file into multiple files that map cleanly onto [Quarto side navigation](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-navigation.html#side-navigation). This is useful when the input document is a single long document that would be better navigated as multiple web pages.
